reconcile.note: Henry treats Matthew's third-person announcement and Mark's second-person address as one voice serving two purposes, notifying John publicly while answering Jesus's own prayer.

discrepancy.note: Strauss notes Mark and Luke's voice addresses Jesus directly in the second person, unlike Matthew's third-person public announcement.

quotes.text: as we see in Matthew: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased…in Mark and Luke, the heavenly voice addresses Jesus in the second person, and by comparing the words which, according to the Fathers, were given in the old and lost gospels as those of the voice.
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined, trans. George Eliot (1846), pt. II, ch. on the baptism of Jesus, on Matthew 3:17 and Mark 1:11.

sides.snippet: This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.
sides.verseText: Behold, a voice out of the heavens said, \"This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.\"

sides.snippet: You are my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.
sides.verseText: A voice came out of the sky, \"You are my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.\"
